note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Partitioning the label's Markov blanket into parents, children, spouses yields identifiable general multi-source domain adaptation (GAMA)

nodes.name: Target joint distribution is underdetermined
nodes.description: Without extra assumptions there are infinitely many joint distributions consistent with source data, so assumptions linking source and target are needed to identify the target joint distribution.

nodes.name: Existing latent methods use restrictive assumptions
nodes.description: Existing latent-representation DA methods rely on restrictive assumptions such as independent latent variables, invariant label distributions or exponential-family distributions, or lack identifiability guarantees for the target joint distribution.

nodes.name: Markov blanket representation is the natural predictive target
nodes.description: The label's Markov blanket (parents, children, spouses) is the minimal predictive set for the label, so a natural approach is to learn a representation of it.

nodes.name: Sufficient-change assumptions across domains
nodes.description: Assumptions 1 and 2 require latent variables' and label's distributions to vary sufficiently across source domains, which makes recovery of latent representations feasible.

nodes.name: Markov blanket subspace is identifiable
nodes.description: Under sufficient changes and faithfulness, modelling the generative process with the minimal number of edges in the learned Markov network recovers a representation that is an invertible transformation of the true Markov blanket (Theorem 1).

nodes.name: Markov blanket alone is underspecified for DA
nodes.description: Because P(Y|Zmb) changes across domains and Y is unavailable in the target, the joint P(Zmb,Y) is not identifiable in the target domain from Markov blanket representations alone.

nodes.name: Parents, children, spouses subspaces identifiable
nodes.description: Under Assumptions 1-3 and faithfulness, the learned Markov blanket can be partitioned into subspaces that are invertible transformations of the true parents, children and spouses of Y (Theorem 2).

nodes.name: Group-specific intimate neighbors assumption
nodes.description: Assumption 3 requires that the intimate neighbors of Y's parents, children and spouses lie only within their own group.

nodes.name: Target factorization via parents and children
nodes.description: With Zpa, Zch, Zsps disentangled, P(Y|X) in the target domain is determined by P(Y|Zpa) and P(Zch|Y,Zsps) in the target (Proposition 1 and Corollary 1).

nodes.name: Low-dimensional change assumption
nodes.description: Assumption 4 confines domain-specific conditional distributions P(Zch|Y=vc,Zsps) to a q-dimensional manifold, so each domain is characterized by mixture weights.

nodes.name: Target joint distribution is identifiable
nodes.description: Under Assumptions 4 and 5 (linear independence), the target distributions P(Zch|Y,Zsps) and P(Y|Zpa) are identifiable, giving identifiability of P(Y|X) in the target domain (Theorem 3, Remark 1).

nodes.name: GAMA models domain-specific parameters with VAEs
nodes.description: GAMA uses VAEs for (theta_Y, Zpa)->Y and (theta_ch, Y, Zsps)->Zch, with a Gumbel-Softmax VAE for discrete Y, plus a classifier; domain parameters theta are learned for the target during training.

nodes.name: GAMA total loss
nodes.description: GAMA trains with Lall = Lcls + l1 Lvae,Z + l2 Lvae,Y + l3 Lvae,Zch + l4 Lch + l5 LY, with beta1 and beta2 set to 1.

nodes.name: Beats strongest baseline on Office-Home
nodes.description: GAMA achieves the best performance in most Office-Home sub-tasks, surpassing the strongest baseline iMSDA by 1% on average (Table 1).

nodes.name: Beats best baseline on PACS
nodes.description: GAMA achieves better average accuracy than the best baseline on PACS, with 98.8% on the Photo domain (Table 1).

nodes.name: Ablation shows VAEs matter
nodes.description: On Office-Home, removing the VAE losses (GAMA-vae) hurts, and the theta-related VAEs further improve accuracy over GAMA-theta (Table 2).

evidence: Sec 1: need identifiability beyond restrictive assumptions

isolated_nodes.name: Datasets and setup
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation uses Office-Home (ResNet50 features, MLP-based VAEs) and PACS (ResNet18 backbone), with one domain as target and the others as sources, averaged over three seeds.

isolated_nodes.name: Special cases of shift
isolated_nodes.description: Restricting changes to the parents of Y is covariate shift, and restricting changes to Y is target (prior probability) shift.

isolated_nodes.name: Faithfulness can be weakened
isolated_nodes.description: Single adjacency-faithfulness and single unshielded-collider-faithfulness suffice in place of full faithfulness, being considerably weaker.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the underdetermination problem and Markov blanket representation to its insufficiency, the finer parent/child/spouse partition, target identifiability, then the GAMA implementation and empirical results.
